newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 6.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

The government today awarded HM Customs and Excise 88 million stg over three years to pay for additional staff to battle tax crime. The new positions will be aimed at tackling fraud and evasion in the import and export of excise goods, tax avoidance and Single Market excise smuggling. The government hopes to yield 2.25 bln in additional revenue.
'EMU DELAY' WORRIES GIVE DOLLAR A BOOST

The dollar strengthened overnight against the Deutschmark and Japanese yen upon rumours of fears that European monetary union may be delayed beyond 1999. This occurred despite Washington concerns over the growing U.S. trade deficit with Japan and fair economic data from Germany.
LLOYD'S SLAMS RESCUE DOOR ON REFUSNIKS

The financial aid package (3.2 billion stg) available to Lloyds Names has been withdrawn to those who are fighting for more financial assistance. Those who did not accept their share of the rescue package lost out as the offer finally closed on Friday.
BATTLE FOR CONTROL AT THE CORE OF APPLE

Apple founder Steve Jobs is returning as a consultant to the firm he helped found 10 years ago. Apple Computer will use the NeXt operating software he designed as opposed to the Copland, the operating system its own engineers had been developing. Gilbert Amelio, the current chief executive is fighting for control of the company.
